subject: Traffic switch play & postmortem next steps
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: ops@acme-retail.com, alice.sre@bigbank.co.uk, brian.park@marketplace.ai
Cc: laura.bennett@redwood.ai, marcus.lin@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 02 Nov 2026 03:12:00 +0000
Subject: Traffic switch play & immediate guidance (EU/APAC impact)

Hi team —

Quick update and immediate customer guidance from Redwood Inference engineering: we detected a degradation in the EU and APAC cloud region peering that is causing elevated token latency and intermittent errors for customers with region affinity to eu-west and apac-south. Our control plane remains healthy; the impact is localized to network egress at two cloud providers.

What we recommend now (immediate, customer-actionable):
- If your integration is region-aware, switch routing to our us-central endpoint (us-central-1) for the next 2–6 hours. This preserves latency for most workloads and avoids the degraded paths. See attached reroute_steps_v1.pdf for step-by-step examples.
- If you use DNS-based zone affinity, update the TTL to 30s and point to host us1.redwood.ai.
- If you need a temporary IP-level bypass, use traffic-config-example.json attached for a canary.

We will:
- Kick off a controlled canary (5% traffic) from 03:45Z to validate cache-warm and KV behavior.
- Monitor token latency and 5xx rate, and pause/rollback the switch immediately if anomalies appear.

Requested actions from you:
1) Confirm you can accept traffic to us-central (reply with YES/NO).
2) If YES, confirm a 30-minute maintenance window for us to start the canary at 03:45Z.
3) Share any pinned model versions that must remain routed to eu/apac (we will honor pinned lanes).

We know this is disruptive — apologies for the interruption. We're treating this as high priority; I will share a running timeline and next steps.

Status link: https://status.redwood.ai/incidents/2026-11-02-traffic-shift
Attachments: reroute_steps_v1.pdf, traffic-config-example.json

—Ben
Ben Carter
Account Lead, Customer Success
Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0147

From: ops@acme-retail.com
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: alice.sre@bigbank.co.uk, james.holt@sre.acme-retail.com
Date: Mon, 02 Nov 2026 03:29:12 +0000
Subject: Re: Traffic switch play & immediate guidance (EU/APAC impact)

Ben — thanks for the heads up. A couple quick clarifying Qs before we flip any traffic: 

1) During the canary, what is the expected degradation window if something goes wrong? (i.e., how quickly can you rollback and what's the blast radius)
2) Our checkout flow uses a pinned model (v5.2.1) in eu-west; can you confirm pinned models will keep using eu endpoints?
3) Do you have any expected cost impact for requests routed to us-central (we need to estimate burst costs)

On the resources side, we can accept routing to us-central for up to 6 hours. We'll wait for your confirmation of start time and the canary size.

—James (on behalf of Acme ops)

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, marcus.lin@redwood.ai
Cc: rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 02 Nov 2026 03:35:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Traffic switch play & immediate guidance (EU/APAC impact)

Ben — I just spoke with infra. Plan below (proposed, please approve):

Planned canary (engineers will execute):
- Start: 03:45Z; size: 5% of traffic for 30 minutes.
- Health checks: latency (p50/p95), 5xx, token-drop rate. Automatic rollback if 5xx > 0.5% or p95 latency > baseline + 200ms over a 5m window.
- If canary passes, escalate to 25% for another 20m then to full shift in 4 steps with 10m observation windows.

Action owners:
- Marcus Lin: kickoff canary and monitor telemetry (on-call).
- Rishi Malhotra: prepare short-circuit rollback script and keep the route map pinned.
- Ben: coordinate with customer (Acme) and confirm pinned model exceptions.

We will honor pinned models—pinned v5.2.1 will remain on eu nodes unless the customer explicitly requests migration. If Acme cannot accept that, we can discuss a managed migration during the maintenance window.

I'll draft a short follow-up to customers with the confirmed start time and quick runbook.

—Laura
Laura Bennett
VP, Platform Reliability
Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: ops@acme-retail.com, alice.sre@bigbank.co.uk, brian.park@marketplace.ai
Cc: laura.bennett@redwood.ai, marcus.lin@redwood.ai, rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 02 Nov 2026 03:40:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Traffic switch play & immediate guidance (EU/APAC impact)

James — thanks for the quick reply and for confirming you can accept routing. We will start the 5% canary at 03:45Z (in ~5 minutes). Expected rollback capability: <3 minutes to revert to the prior routing map; blast radius limited to canary participants. Cost: some tokens routed to us-central may see a modest increase; we'll share an estimate after the canary results but expect <8% bill change for routed traffic during the window.

Quick canary runbook (high level):
1) Redwood will update route map to send 5% of Acme's traffic to us-central at 03:45Z.
2) Acme: watch your checkout flows and notify us immediately if you see errors (contact + direct SRE line below).
3) Redwood will pause/pulse on any abnormal telemetry and roll back within 3 minutes if thresholds breached.

Contact: incident Slack: #inc-2026-1102 (redwood-infra); on-call Marcus Lin +1 (415) 555-0199.

If anything changes we will notify you on the status page and follow up with a full postmortem.

Attachments: reroute_steps_v1.pdf, traffic-config-example.json

—Ben

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
To: ben.carter@redwood.ai, marcus.lin@redwood.ai, rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai
Cc: ben.carter@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 03 Nov 2026 18:45:00 +0000
Subject: Postmortem draft: Regional egress degradation (EU & APAC) — timeline, root cause, action items

Team — draft postmortem below to share internally and with affected customers tomorrow. Please review and flag edits. I will publish the redacted customer-facing postmortem by 09:00Z.

Summary:
On 2026-11-02 02:58Z we observed a sharp increase in token latency and 5xx errors for requests served through two cloud providers' peering paths in EU and APAC. The root cause was an incorrect BGP export policy on the provider edge that caused asymmetric routing for a subset of egress prefixes; during high-concurrency KV cache churn this produced transient failures and elevated latency.

Impact:
- Affected regions: eu-west (primary) and apac-south (secondary).
- Customer-facing impact window: ~02:58Z – 04:10Z with partial mitigation from the traffic switch starting at 03:45Z.
- Severity: P2 for most customers; P1 for a small subset with pinned eu-only models.

Timeline (high level):
- 02:58Z — spike in p95 latency and token 5xx alerted.
- 03:12Z — customer communications sent (initial notice).
- 03:35Z — infra confirms asymmetric routing hypothesis; canary plan created.
- 03:45Z — 5% canary started to us-central.
- 03:52Z — canary passed; progressive shift to 25% then full as telemetry allowed.
- 04:10Z — major error rates returned to baseline for routed traffic.

Root cause analysis:
- Primary: provider-level BGP export misconfiguration that only impacted specific egress prefixes under particular concurrency patterns.
- Contributing: our KV cache churn under high concurrent warm-start requests increased sensitivity to asymmetric paths.

Action items (owners & due dates):
1) Provider remediation confirmation — Platform Partnerships (Assigned: Marcus Lin) — due 2026-11-06.
2) Build routing-drift detector tuned to egress asymmetry (Assigned: Rishi Malhotra) — due 2026-11-20.
3) Extend traffic-redirect runbooks and pre-built templates for common customers (Assigned: Ben Carter) — due 2026-11-09.
4) Add pinned-model migration tooling to allow safe, automated cross-region moves (Assigned: Reliability PM) — due 2026-12-01.

Customer comms plan: publish a redacted postmortem to affected customers tomorrow with root cause, what we changed, and the action items + ETA. Keep pinned-model customers in a separate notice and offer a managed migration if needed.

Attachments: postmortem-draft.docx

—Laura
Laura Bennett
VP, Platform Reliability
Redwood Inference
